plugins.name: isolated-review
plugins.description: TAKT-based isolated code review. Runs each review perspective (correctness, regression, tests, security + overall) as an independent read-only session, consolidates findings in a dedicated integration session, and formats the result without changing verdicts.

plugins.name: light-review
plugins.description: Cognitive-load-light PR review. Findings are written as an inverted pyramid — one-line conclusion, minimal evidence, the fix, the impact, what still needs checking — with the severity-swinging context embedded in the finding itself; the spots confirmed OK keep the full waterfall so the reasons for approval stay on record. Code-smell centric, no TAKT.

plugins.name: health-checkup
plugins.description: Periodic repository health checkup. Counts — never blocks — the obligations offloaded during development: unresolved TODOs, "guaranteed elsewhere" claims classified as verified / missing / untraceable, stale and unmilestoned issues, coverage, and spec-implementation drift. An LLM only extracts where a claim points; scripts decide whether that place exists, do the arithmetic, and append the numbers next to their baselines. The diagnosis is left to humans. It also counts the tests that do not test: the ones switched off without a tracked reason, the ones that cannot fail (no assertion, an assertion true by construction, or the subject itself mocked away), and the places where the suite is kept green by configuration rather than by tests — failures coverage cannot show, because a skipped test barely moves the rate and a test that cannot fail raises it.

plugins.name: pr-loop
plugins.description: Loops that keep the PR queue moving. They own the ordering, the repetition and its ceilings, and the exit — not the review itself, which is delegated to light-review / isolated-review. codex-draft-review takes a codex-authored draft PR to human-review-ready and never merges; the verdict stays with the human. bot-pr-resolve routes a Dependabot / Renovate / security PR by class and merges only when every safety criterion holds. merge-ready-sweep merges what a human already approved, reading the bar from branch protection instead of assuming one, and refusing an approval that predates the current head. review-wait-resolve takes a PR stuck waiting on a human and moves it by why it is stuck — no reviewer, review not started, changes requested and left, or rotted past usefulness. One PR per invocation; the outer iteration belongs to /loop. Needs nothing but gh.

plugins.name: worker-fleet
plugins.description: Supervisor-side loops that run development through Claude worker sessions. issue-ready-prep is the human-present step: before an issue reaches Ready it fills in what request-create will ask — work type, goal, background, acceptance criteria, slug, and the base branch — and writes them into the issue as a machine-readable block, which raises Ready from "someone may start this" to "this can be started unattended". issue-to-review-ready then runs unattended: it takes one prepared Ready issue, moves it to In progress before touching anything, answers request-create from the prepared values rather than guessing, stands up a worker in its own worktree, confirms the draft PR exists rather than trusting the report, hands the review to codex-draft-review, verifies the undraft and reviewer assignment, advances the board, and moves to the next issue — and if it stops anywhere, it puts the status back, because an issue parked in In progress is worse than an untouched one. worker-fleet-loop adds the parallel case: one tick sweeps every worker, answering approvals (everything except merge), nudging the silent, and dispatching one new lane into capacity measured fresh each tick. The implementation belongs to openspec-workflow and the review to pr-loop; this plugin owns the lane.
